messages.body:
Re-flagging the date-field thing — I cannot start frontend
integration tests until we have a decision. ISO-8601 UTC on the
API is non-negotiable from my side because partners are integrating.
Confirmed on my end — ISO-8601 UTC is locked in the eng spec (v2) and I'm actively working AUDIT-5. On track for t=4320. Will flag immediately if anything changes.

@priya — the ISO-8601 UTC decision is already confirmed and locked (see task comments on AUDIT-5 and the decision doc). No further debate needed. The API returns ISO-8601 UTC; frontend handles localisation. You are unblocked to proceed with frontend integration tests on that basis. See you at the spec review at t=4500 to close out any remaining open items.

Jumping in here — the API format (ISO-8601 UTC) being locked is fine for partner integrations. But the PRD still specifies that **customer-facing UI surfaces display dates in the user's local time**, and that hasn't been explicitly overridden. Those are two separate decisions. I'm not blocking AUDIT-5, but I do need a documented decision on the UI date display before I can sign off on AUDIT-1. Can we make sure that's on the agenda for the spec review at t=4500?

Sam is right that these are two separate decisions, and they're not in conflict. API contract = ISO-8601 UTC (locked). UI display = localised to user's timezone (frontend concern, always has been). The PRD's localised format spec applies to the UI layer, not the API response. I'll make sure that's explicit in the eng spec so AUDIT-1 sign-off is straightforward. See everyone at t=4500.

Agreed — these are orthogonal decisions and there's no conflict. API contract is ISO-8601 UTC (locked in eng spec v2). UI localisation is a frontend concern and the PRD's localised display spec applies there, not to the API response. I'll add an explicit note to the eng spec clarifying the boundary before t=4500 so AUDIT-1 sign-off is clean.

Glad we're aligned. To be explicit: the PRD has always specified localised date display on customer-facing surfaces, and that hasn't changed — it's a UI-layer requirement, fully orthogonal to the API contract. I'll be at the spec review at t=4500 and will not sign off on AUDIT-1 until the localised UI display decision is explicitly documented. Priya, thanks for adding the boundary note to the eng spec — that'll make it clean.

And I cannot in good conscience ship a customer surface that shows
UTC timestamps to non-engineers. We need a PM call here.

@sam — the audit spec review just wrapped. Here's the documented outcome on both decisions:

1. **API contract**: ISO-8601 UTC — locked. Priya has this in eng spec v2.
2. **UI date display**: Customer-facing surfaces display dates in the user's local timezone — this is the PRD requirement and has never changed. It is now explicitly documented as a UI-layer concern, separate from the API contract.

These are orthogonal decisions, both now formally resolved. Sam, this should unblock your AUDIT-1 sign-off. Priya, please confirm the eng spec has the boundary note added.

Morgan — I'll follow up separately with the full audit-log status update.

Good to see both decisions locked down cleanly. TPM — I'll be watching for that audit-log status update since three deals are gated on this feature shipping in v2.4. If there's any risk to the timeline, I need to know ASAP so I can manage customer expectations.

Confirmed — eng spec v2 has the boundary note: API contract is ISO-8601 UTC, UI localisation is a frontend concern handled at the display layer. Both decisions are cleanly separated. AUDIT-1 should be clear for sign-off.

Thanks for the clear write-up. Both decisions match what the PRD has always said, and the boundary note in the eng spec is exactly what I needed to see documented. AUDIT-1 has my sign-off — customers get localised dates, API stays ISO-8601 UTC, clean separation. Let's ship it.
Great — glad we got there. API stays ISO-8601 UTC, UI localisation lives in the frontend, boundary is documented. Eng team is clear to proceed. Let's ship.

**Audit-log decisions — documented ✅**

To close the loop from the spec review:

1. **API contract**: ISO-8601 UTC — locked. Priya has this in eng spec v2.
2. **UI date display**: Localised to user's timezone — locked. PRD localised display spec applies to the UI layer only, orthogonal to the API contract.

These two decisions are explicit and non-conflicting. Sam, this should unblock your AUDIT-1 sign-off. Priya, please confirm the boundary note is in the eng spec so we can close AUDIT-1 cleanly.

@person.morgan — t=5000 is still our hard wall. Both decisions are clean; no slippage risk visible right now.
